rationale: The principle is a narrow empirical boundary claim about communication-channel reset frequency in multi-agent collaboration, tested in a specific environment (WhoDunitEnv with 20 suspects). None of the candidate meta-principles operate on the same variables, conditions, scale, or epistemic type. Candidates such as channel capacity, test-time compute, information cascades, working memory, and benchmark saturation are semantically suggestive but do not entail or constrain the effect of repeated communication resets. The relation direction and condition compatibility are insufficient for any grounded link. The claim may be sound as a study-bound empirical result, but no compatible foundational meta-principle is available in the supplied set.
